extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance on handling prosecution after a final rejection: interviews, after-final replies/amendments, notices of appeal, examiner amendments, Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs), AFCP 2.0, and QPIDS. Focused on timing, eligibility, what may be entered, and examiner actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for after-final interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews may be conducted after the expiration of SSP for reply to a final office action but within the 6-month statutory period for reply (without the payment of an extension fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 706.07(f)(III). Example: interviews are allowable after SSP expiration so long as within the 6-month statutory reply period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on number/condition of after-final interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, one interview after final rejection may be granted if the examiner is convinced that disposal or clarification for appeal may be accomplished with only nominal further consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 713.09. Examiner should evaluate whether only nominal further consideration is necessary before granting an interview after final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner participation requirements for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews (personal and telephone) must include an examiner who has negotiation authority, and who is familiar with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 713.05. Interviews lacking an examiner with negotiation authority or familiarity are not proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant reply options after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid abandonment, applicant’s reply options are: filing an after final reply (37 CFR 1.116); appealing any rejections (37 CFR 41.31); or filing an RCE (37 CFR 1.114).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 706.07 and 714.13(II). Applicants must choose among these limited pathways; other unrestricted prosecution is not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: No right to unrestricted further prosecution after a proper final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a proper final rejection has been entered in an application, applicant or patent owner no longer has any right to unrestricted further prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.116 applies to replies filed after final action and prior to appeal. Ordinarily, amendments filed after final action are not entered unless approved by the examiner. MPEP 714.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory action when after-final reply not placing application in condition for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the after final reply does not place the application in condition for allowance, an advisory action (PTOL-303) should be sent to the applicant stating the remaining period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no notice of appeal was filed, normally the reply period continues to run 3 months from the mailing date of the final rejection plus any paid extensions. If the advisory action is mailed more than 3 months after the final rejection in response to an after-final reply filed within 2 months of the final rejection, the SSP ends on the mailing date of the advisory action (variable reply period considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-month statutory reply period limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory period for reply will never expire later than six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: interplay of filing date, advisory action mailing date, and extension availability; applicant required to pay full extension even when only part of that extension is usable due to the six-month statutory limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final amendments are not entered as a matter of right
rubrics_metrics.description: After final replies can include an after final amendment under 37 CFR 1.116, but 1.116 is much more restrictive than 1.111 (replies to non-final office actions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant can present an amendment after final rejection to file an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114. In rare instances, amendments may be presented after the mailing of an examiner’s answer and prior to the fee to forward an appeal to the Board to cancel appealed claims or where examiner is convinced some claims are in condition for allowance. MPEP 714.13(II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of allowing after-final amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow applicant to present certain types of amendments after prosecution is closed to reduce pendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy contemplates that within the statutory period for response, the case may be put in either condition for allowance or better condition for appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of after-final amendments that may be entered
rubrics_metrics.description: The types of after final amendments that may be entered are: (1) to cancel claims or comply with any requirement of form expressly set forth in a previous action; (2) to present rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal; and (3) an amendment touching the merits upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the amendment is necessary and was not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.116(b)(1),(2),(3) and MPEP 714.13(II). Note: If an examiner can readily determine a proposed amendment will place the application in condition for allowance, the final amendment may be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final amendments are either entered or not entered (not 'entered in part')
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments after final are either 'entered' or 'not entered.' They are NOT 'entered in part.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If part of the amendment would be acceptable, notify applicant which portions would be acceptable for better form for appeal, to comply with objections/requirements as to form, render certain claims allowable, or to make an examiner’s amendment. MPEP 714.12, 714.13, and 714.20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action when after-final amendment not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: If the after final amendment or submission does not place the claims in condition for allowance or in better form for appeal, an advisory action (PTOL-303) should be sent out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 714.13(III), 706.07(f). The advisory action should explain reasons and remaining period for reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplary reasons for non-entry of after-final amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons include: the amendment does not place the application in better form for appeal; the claims as amended would raise new matter (identify new matter); the claims as amended present new issues requiring further consideration or search; the amendment presents additional claims without canceling finally rejected claims and does not place the application in better condition for appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 714.13(III), 706.07(f). These are typical reasons to include on PTOL-303 advisory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of affidavits or evidence after final
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or other evidence may be admitted after final rejection upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons as to why it is necessary and was not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.116(e) and MPEP 714.13. Examiner should assess whether the 'good and sufficient reasons' standard is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special case — entering amendment with proposed rejection(s) for appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of appeal, proposed amendment(s) will be entered and proposed rejection(s) will be included in the examiner’s answer; such rejections must be addressed in any brief on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FP 7.169 Advisory Action, Proposed Rejection of Claims, Before Appeal Brief. When amendments are entered for appeal, the examiner will specify what claims would be rejected and on what grounds in the examiner’s answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of filings determines which regulation governs entry of after-final amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appeal is filed after a final rejection, the order of filing an after final amendment, notice of appeal, and appeal brief determines whether 37 CFR 1.116 or 41.33 controls the entry of the after final amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful attention to timing of amendment vs appeal brief is required; different rules apply depending on sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of after-final amendment filed with or after appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: An after final amendment filed before the appeal brief is treated under 37 CFR 1.116. An amendment filed with or after the appeal brief is treated under 37 CFR 41.33(b) and may only be entered to cancel claims (without affecting scope of other claims) or rewrite dependent claims into independent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 41.33(b) restricts the types of post-brief amendments that may be entered for appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same-day filing of amendment, notice of appeal, and appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant files an after final amendment, a notice of appeal, and an appeal brief on the same date after the mailing of a final action, 37 CFR 1.116 applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing rule exception: same-day filings are treated under 1.116 per the guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner-initiated interviews to expedite allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner is aware of claim amendments that would place the application in condition for allowance, there may be an opportunity for an examiner-initiated interview to expedite allowance and facilitate compact prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should consider initiating interviews when amendments appear to resolve issues and lead to allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and uses of examiner's amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner's amendments are typically used to cancel or amend claims, and to make formal corrections to the application, including the drawings and the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be signed by a primary examiner and authorized by applicant in a formal interview (personal or telephone). If examiner amends drawings, applicant must provide replacement drawings reflecting changes. MPEP 1302.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendments — extension of time when complete first reply within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete first reply to a final office action filed within 2 months: an examiner’s amendment to place the application in condition for allowance may be made without the payment of extension fees even if made more than 3 months from the date of the final office action. However, an examiner’s amendment cannot be made after the 6-month statutory time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 706.07(f)(II). Timing of the applicant’s initial after-final reply affects extension fee requirements for examiner’s amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendments — extension of time when complete first reply filed after 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: For a complete first reply filed after 2 months: applicant’s authorization to make an amendment to place the application in condition for allowance must be made either within the 3-month SSP or within an extended period for reply that has been petitioned and paid for by applicant pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, an examiner’s amendment correcting only formal matters identified for the first time after a reply to a final office action would not require any extension fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendments — petition or deposit-account authorization for necessary extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an extension of time not to exceed the 6-month statutory period is necessary to place an application in condition for allowance, applicant may file the required petition and fee or give authorization to the examiner to make the petition of record and charge a specified fee to a deposit account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use procedural form FP 13.02.02 to effectuate deposit-account authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte Quayle for formal matters identified after reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal matters identified for the first time after a reply to a final office action which require applicant action to correct may be required to be corrected in an Ex parte Quayle action if the application is otherwise in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extension fees would be required. Consider an examiner’s amendment instead of an Ex parte Quayle to resolve formal matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE definition — what an RCE is
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE is a procedure under 37 CFR 1.114 under which an applicant may obtain continued examination of an application in which prosecution is closed (final rejection, appeal, notice of allowance, or action that otherwise closes prosecution). An RCE is not the filing of a new application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 706.07(h). If timely filed with submission and fee, the office will withdraw the finality of any office action and the submission will be entered and considered (37 CFR 1.114).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE availability — what applications qualify
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies to utility or plant applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995; or international applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995 that comply with 35 U.S.C. 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP references; check filing basis and dates to determine RCE eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE non-applicability — what does not qualify
rubrics_metrics.description: Does not apply to: provisional applications; applications filed under 111(a) before June 8, 1995; international applications filed under 363 before June 8, 1995 or not complying with 371; applications for a design patent or international design application; or patents under reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult MPEP for precise list and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filing conditions/timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may obtain continued examination by filing PTO/SB/30, a submission and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) prior to the earliest of: payment of the issue fee (unless a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 is granted), abandonment of the application, or filing of a notice of appeal to the CAFC or commencement of civil action challenging a PTAB affirmance (unless terminated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 706.07. Timing is critical — once those events occur, RCE may no longer be available.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE — first action final after filing RCE (when proper)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims of an RCE application may be finally rejected in the action immediately subsequent to the filing of the RCE where all claims after entry are either identical to or patentably indistinct from the pre-RCE claims, and would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next office action if entered prior to the RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 706.07(b). Examiner may make a final rejection immediately if the RCE does not introduce material that would avoid finality.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE — circumstances when making first office action final is improper
rubrics_metrics.description: It would not be proper to make final a first office action in an RCE where that application contains material presented after final rejection but denied entry because new issues were raised requiring further consideration/search or the issue of new matter was raised. Also improper if the first office action includes a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 706.07(b) and 706.07(h)(VIII). Examiner must examine whether the RCE introduces new issues or art that require more than routine consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE submission requirement — what must be included
rubrics_metrics.description: Must include a reply to the final rejection that meets the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111 (e.g., an amendment filed with the RCE or a previously-filed after final amendment). Mere request for RCE and payment of the fee is not sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission can be an amendment to the specification/claims/drawings, new arguments, new evidence in support of patentability, or an IDS in an application subject to a notice of allowance (but not where last action is a final rejection or Ex parte Quayle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of RCE submission not being a bona fide reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: (a) a reply to a final office action includes submission of IDS only; (b) an amendment that would cancel all of the claims in an application without any new or substitute claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions are not sufficient to avoid abandonment even if RCE fee paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of bona fide RCE reply that is not fully responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: (1) a non-compliant amendment (not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121); (2) presentation of claims for a different invention (applicant cannot switch inventions), e.g., cancelling elected invention claims and presenting only claims to a non-elected invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These may be bona fide attempts but raise issues of compliance or inventive subject matter that examiners must address.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE after Ex parte Quayle or after allowance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: After Ex parte Quayle action: must include a reply to the Ex parte Quayle action. After allowance: RCE submission may include an IDS, amendment, new arguments, or new evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 706.07(h)(II). Ensure required reply is included depending on the closing action being reopened.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after appeal but before decision by the Board — requirements and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Must include a reply to the final rejection (may incorporate previously filed appeal brief). Filing of an RCE will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution before the examiner, regardless of whether the RCE is proper or improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.114(d) and MPEP 706.07(h)(X). For an improper RCE after appeal: if no claim is allowed, application is abandoned; allowed claims except for their dependency from rejected claims treated as rejected; if at least one allowed claim, pass to issue or allow correction of formal matters within two months.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE after Board decision and after appeal to CAFC
rubrics_metrics.description: Within sixty-three days of the decision by the Board (but before filing of a notice of appeal to the CAFC or commencement of a civil action): for a proper RCE, appeal is withdrawn and prosecution is reopened; for an improper RCE, send PTOL-90 with FP 07.42.16. After appeal to the CAFC or civil action, RCE not available unless the appeal/civil action is terminated and application is still pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 706.07(h)(XI)-(XII). Examiner should consult SPE or QAS when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: AFCP 2.0 — ability to request additional consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of submitting an after final amendment under 37 CFR 1.116, applicant may additionally request additional consideration under the After Final Consideration Pilot (AFCP 2.0). Examiner can get up to 3 hours non-production time to perform additional examination to determine allowability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AFCP 2.0 aims to reduce pendency by increasing applications allowed after final and reducing RCEs. Applicant applies using Form PTO/SB/434 or equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: AFCP 2.0 — eligibility and application limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must: have an outstanding final rejection; have been filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or 371(c); have a request for AFCP 2.0; amend at least one independent claim that does not broaden the scope of that claim in any aspect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one AFCP 2.0 request may be filed in response to an outstanding final rejection. Include a statement that applicant is willing and available to participate in an examiner-initiated interview concerning the response.

rubrics_metrics.name: AFCP 2.0 — incomplete or disqualifying submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If submission is incomplete or request is improper, examiner should process the after final submission under 37 CFR 1.116 (pre-pilot practice). If request qualifies, examiner determines whether additional search/consideration would be required and is possible within AFCP 2.0 time allotment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors (not exhaustive) that might require more time: claims added, complexity of amendment, at least one added claim directed to a different invention (possible restriction), prior after final interviews or traditional after final submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: AFCP 2.0 — examiner actions and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: If no additional search/consideration is needed or can be completed in time, examiner will consider whether the amendment places the application in condition for allowance. If it does, the examiner will enter the amendment and mail a notice of allowance; if not, the examiner will request an interview with the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner has up to 3 hours of non-production time under the pilot to carry out additional examination as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: QPIDS general purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick Path IDS (QPIDS) is designed to allow applicant submissions of prior art after a final office action, after the mailing of a notice of allowance, and even after the payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If QPIDS submitted after payment of the issue fee, an RCE must be filed with the QPIDS but will not be processed unless the art necessitates reopening prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: QPIDS — Path 0 requirements (IDS after final rejection and prior to disposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Path 0 (IDS filed after a final rejection and prior to disposal) requires: IDS, IDS fee, Certification under 37 CFR 1.97(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow standard IDS practice and certifications when filing after final but prior to disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: QPIDS — Path 1 requirements (IDS after notice of allowance and prior to or with issue fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Path 1 (IDS filed after mailing of a notice of allowance and prior to or with payment of the issue fee) requires: IDS, IDS fee, Certification under 37 CFR 1.97(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should provide the same certifications and fees as required for typical IDS submissions in this window.

rubrics_metrics.name: QPIDS — Path 2 requirements (IDS after payment of issue fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Path 2 (IDS filed after payment of the issue fee) requires: PTO/SB/09 Form ("QPIDS.REC" in IFW), IDS, IDS fee, Certification under 37 CFR 1.97(e), Web ePetition to withdraw from issue and petition fee, RCE (PTO/SB/30) and RCE fee, and authorization to charge all fees associated with the QPIDS to a USPTO deposit account (included on PTO/SB/09 Form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All specified forms/fees/authorizations must be included; an RCE filed with QPIDS will not be processed unless the art necessitates reopening prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary — topics examiners should master after final
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners (and applicants) should be familiar with: after final interviews, after final replies, notices of appeal, examiner's amendments, handling RCEs, AFCP 2.0, and QPIDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slide deck concluded list of topics as key learning objectives and provides examiner/external resource links for deeper details.
